prompt: Why does Cine Aurora handle Célia’s requests on a Kanban board rather than in sprints?

choices.text: Kanban needs no testing
choices.why: Testing is a column on the board.

choices.text: Célia’s requests are too large to fit into a two-week sprint
choices.why: Most of them are small.

choices.text: Scrum forbids fixing defects
choices.why: It forbids nothing of the kind.

choices.text: They arrive any day, and some cannot wait two weeks
choices.why: Right: a stream of small, unplanned work fits flow better than a fixed cycle.

prompt: Why is "waiting for test" drawn as a column of its own?
hint: Who is working on a card there?

choices.text: It holds the cards a tester has rejected and sent back to the developer who built them
choices.why: It holds cards that are built and not yet tested.

choices.text: It makes the wait visible
choices.why: Right: nobody works on a card there, and the column shows the queue.

choices.text: It is where testing happens
choices.why: Testing has its own column next to it.

choices.text: Kanban requires exactly five columns
choices.why: A team draws whatever steps it has.

prompt: What does the word kanban mean in Japanese?
hint: Toyota used them to control production.

choices.text: A card
choices.why: Right: a signboard or card.

choices.text: Continuous flow
choices.why: That is what it is used for, not what the word means.

choices.text: Stop the line
choices.why: That idea is jidoka.

choices.text: A production line in a car factory
choices.why: No.

prompt: Which of these are core practices of the Kanban method? Choose all that apply.
hint: Six of them, in Anderson’s list.

choices.text: visualise the work
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: limit work in progress
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: make policies explicit
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: fixed two-week sprints
choices.why: No: Kanban has no sprints.

prompt: A board holds 9 cards on average and 3 cards a week reach done. On average, how many weeks does a card spend on the board?
The team cuts the board to 6 cards on average. Throughput stays at 3 a week. What is the new average time on the board, in weeks?
Another team finishes 4 cards a week and its cards spend 2 weeks on the board on average. How many cards are on its board on average?
hint: Turn the law around: work in progress = time × throughput.

prompt: "Waiting for test" is full at its limit of two, and Rafael has just finished building a card. What should he do?

choices.text: Raise the limit on "waiting for test" to three, just for this week
choices.why: A limit that moves whenever it bites is a decoration.

choices.text: Help a card in testing move, by pairing with Lia
choices.why: Right: the limit turns testing into the whole team’s problem.

choices.text: Start the next card in "ready"
choices.why: That is the starting the limit exists to stop.

choices.text: Move his card into "waiting for test" anyway
choices.why: The column is full; the rule says no.

prompt: By Little’s law, which is usually the faster way to shorten the time a card spends on the board?
hint: One of them is a decision the team can take tomorrow.

choices.text: Add more columns to the board
choices.why: More columns do not change the arithmetic.

choices.text: Ask everybody to work longer hours every week until the queue is gone
choices.why: The law points at the cards, not the hours.

choices.text: Hold fewer cards in progress
choices.why: Right: nobody has to work faster.

choices.text: Hire more people
choices.why: That raises throughput, slowly and expensively.

prompt: The testing column is full every single day for a month. What does that tell the team?

choices.text: Testing is where the flow is slowest
choices.why: Right: automate more checks, make cards smaller, or share the testing.

choices.text: Lia works too slowly
choices.why: A queue is a property of how work is organised.

choices.text: The limit is working, so nothing needs to change
choices.why: The limit has done its job: it has shown where to act.

choices.text: The column should be removed
choices.why: That would hide the queue again.

prompt: Match each flow measure to what it counts.

pairs.right: from the start of work to done

prompt: A card spends 2 days building, 5 waiting for test, 1 testing and 1 waiting to be released. What is its flow efficiency, as a percentage, to the nearest whole number?
In March everybody said "testing is slow". What did counting the days show?
hint: One day, and five before it.

choices.text: Building was the slowest step, at five days for every card
choices.why: Building took two days.

choices.text: Lia had been testing each card three or four times over
choices.why: Testing took one day per card.

choices.text: Testing took one day; the five before it were a queue
choices.why: Right: a queue is about organisation, not speed.

choices.text: Testing took five days
choices.why: Those were the days waiting for test.

prompt: On a cumulative flow diagram, one band keeps getting thicker while its neighbours stay thin. What does it mean?
hint: Thickness is how many cards are in the column.

choices.text: The team is finishing more work than it starts
choices.why: Finished work is the bottom band.

choices.text: The diagram was drawn with the wrong scale on its vertical axis
choices.why: Nothing is wrong with the drawing.

choices.text: A queue is growing in that column
choices.why: Right: cards come in faster than they go out.

choices.text: That column is the fastest
choices.why: The opposite.

prompt: A manager tells the team to halve its lead time by next month. What is the danger this lesson names?

choices.text: The team will work too fast
choices.why: Speed is not the danger named.

choices.text: Lead time cannot be measured on a board that has no sprints
choices.why: It can; the table measures it.

choices.text: Throughput will rise too high
choices.why: No.

choices.text: Cards are moved to done before they are tested
choices.why: Right: the diagram looks wonderful and says nothing about quality.

prompt: What is a policy on a Kanban board?
hint: Written at the top of the column.

choices.text: The number of cards allowed in a column
choices.why: That is the limit.

choices.text: The order of the columns
choices.why: No.

choices.text: A document describing the company’s attitude to quality, kept by the manager
choices.why: It is on the board, where everybody sees it.

choices.text: The rule for leaving a column
choices.why: Right: the definition of done, split by column.

prompt: Rafael asks whether a one-line fix may skip "testing". How does the board answer?

choices.text: Yes: small changes are the exception
choices.why: Nothing on the board says so.

choices.text: Only through the expedite lane, which is meant for small fixes
choices.why: The expedite lane still goes through testing.

choices.text: No: no column says "unless it is small"
choices.why: Right: the policy settled the argument before it started.

choices.text: Yes, if Lia agrees
choices.why: The policies have no exception for that.

prompt: What is jidoka?

choices.text: Stopping the line where a defect appears
choices.why: Right: fixed where it appears, not passed down the line.

choices.text: A card that asks the previous station for more parts
choices.why: That is the kanban card.

choices.text: A limit on work in progress
choices.why: A different idea.

choices.text: A report of the defects found at the end of each month on the line
choices.why: The point is not to wait for the end.

prompt: Why does a blocked card stay in its column and count against the limit?

choices.text: So the column fills and the problem becomes everybody’s
choices.why: Right: that is stopping the line, on a board.

choices.text: So that it can be forgotten
choices.why: The opposite.

choices.text: Because blocked cards are moved to done
choices.why: No.

choices.text: Because the board has nowhere else to put it
choices.why: A board could have a column for it; staying put is deliberate.

prompt: Cine Aurora’s expedite lane allows one card at a time. Why does that second rule matter?

choices.text: Without it, the lane becomes the board
choices.why: Right: everything becomes urgent.

choices.text: Only one person can test urgent cards
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: Urgent cards skip testing
choices.why: They do not.

choices.text: The board is too narrow to draw a second card in the lane
choices.why: No.

prompt: At the morning stand-up, the team walks the board in a set order. Put the columns in that order.
hint: Right to left: finishing before starting.
trap: The cards nearest done come first.

prompt: A team has a board, columns and nothing else. Which change does this lesson say will make the most difference to testing?
hint: Visualising on its own changes little.

choices.text: More colours for the cards
choices.why: Still only visualising.

choices.text: Two-week sprints
choices.why: That is Scrum, not Kanban.

choices.text: A bigger board
choices.why: No.

choices.text: A limit on each column, so queues cannot grow
choices.why: Right: the limit is what makes the board a method.
